title: Put it together
summary: Use everything from the week in new situations.

steps.title: Everything at once
steps.body: Today mixes everything from the week: checking what fits, keeping a running total, splitting, tracking a goal, choosing and handling changes. Take each step on its own.
steps.example: Kai gets {m:1200}. Kai puts {m:400} in Save and keeps {m:800} in Spend, then buys a {m:300} snack. Spend now has {m:500}, and Save still has {m:400}.

steps.prompt: Kai has {m:650} in Spend. Which pair could Kai buy together?

options.text: A cap for {m:300} and a book for {m:400}
options.feedback: Not quite. Together those cost {m:700}, which is more than {m:650}.

options.text: A keyring for {m:250} and a comic for {m:350}
options.feedback: Yes. Together they cost {m:600}, which fits in {m:650}.

options.text: A game for {m:500} and a pen for {m:200}
options.feedback: Not quite. Together those cost {m:700}, which is more than {m:650}.

hints: Add the two prices in each pair.
Only one pair comes to less than {m:650}.
steps.correct: Nice. That's it. {m:600} fits, with {m:50} to spare.

replay.prompt: Noor has {m:900} in Spend. Which pair could Noor buy together?

options.text: A scarf for {m:450} and a book for {m:500}
options.feedback: Not quite. Together those cost {m:950}, which is more than {m:900}.

options.text: A game for {m:600} and a snack for {m:350}
options.feedback: Not quite. Together those cost {m:950}, which is more than {m:900}.

options.text: A T-shirt for {m:400} and a puzzle for {m:450}
options.feedback: Yes. Together they cost {m:850}, which fits in {m:900}.

hints: Add the two prices in each pair.
Only one pair comes to less than {m:900}.
replay.correct: Nice. That's it. {m:850} fits, with {m:50} to spare.

steps.prompt: Kai takes {m:800} to a school fair and buys a cake for {m:150}, a badge for {m:200} and a plant for {m:250}. What's left?

misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. That adds everything. Each buy takes money away.
Not quite. That's what Kai spent. Take it away from {m:800}.

steps.wrong: Not quite. Add the three buys, then take the total away from {m:800}.
hints: Keep a running total of the three buys.
The buys come to {m:600}. Take that away from {m:800}.
steps.correct: That's it. The buys come to {m:600}, so {m:200} is left.

replay.prompt: Noor takes {m:1000} to a book sale and buys three books for {m:150}, {m:250} and {m:300}. What's left?

misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. That adds everything. Each buy takes money away.
Not quite. That's what Noor spent. Take it away from {m:1000}.

replay.wrong: Not quite. Add the three books, then take the total away from {m:1000}.
hints: Keep a running total of the three books.
The books come to {m:700}. Take that away from {m:1000}.
replay.correct: That's it. The books come to {m:700}, so {m:300} is left.

steps.prompt: Kai gets a {m:1600} birthday gift. Split it so at least half goes to Save.
steps.wrong: Not quite. Save has less than half. Split {m:1600} into two equal parts to find half.
hints: Half means two equal parts.
Half of {m:1600} is half of {m:1000} plus half of {m:600}.
steps.correct: Nice. That's it. At least half is in Save, and the rest is in Spend.

replay.prompt: Ari gets a {m:1400} birthday gift. Split it so at least half goes to Save.
replay.wrong: Not quite. Save has less than half. Split {m:1400} into two equal parts to find half.
hints: Half means two equal parts.
Half of {m:1400} is half of {m:1000} plus half of {m:400}.
replay.correct: Nice. That's it. At least half is in Save, and the rest is in Spend.

steps.prompt: Kai's goal costs {m:5000}. Kai has {m:2500} in Save. How far along is Kai?

options.feedback: Not quite. A quarter of {m:5000} is {m:1250}. Kai has more than that.
Not quite. Kai still needs another {m:2500}, the same again.

hints: Compare {m:2500} with {m:5000}.
How many times does {m:2500} fit into {m:5000}?
steps.correct: Nice. That's it. Halfway, with {m:2500} still to go.

replay.prompt: Remi's goal costs {m:4000}. Remi has {m:1000} in Save. How far along is Remi?

options.feedback: Not quite. Half of {m:4000} is {m:2000}. Remi has less than that.
Not quite. Remi still needs another {m:3000}.

hints: Compare {m:1000} with {m:4000}.
How many times does {m:1000} fit into {m:4000}?
replay.correct: Nice. That's it. A quarter of the way, with {m:3000} still to go.

steps.prompt: Kai has a busy week coming up. Sort each thing into need or want.

items.text: A calculator Kai's teacher asked for
A swim cap Kai's club says to wear
A new game for the weekend
School shoes, as Kai's old ones are too tight

steps.wrong: Not quite. Ask: does Kai have to have it this week? If not, it's a want.
hints: Which ones has someone said Kai must have, or can Kai not do without?
Fun extras are wants, even really good ones.
steps.correct: All sorted. The needs are what Kai has to have. The rest are wants Kai can choose.

steps.prompt: Kai saves {m:500} a week and needs 6 more weeks. Then a {m:500} gift goes into Save. When does Kai finish?

options.feedback: Not quite. The gift adds to Save, so Kai needs less.
Not quite. {m:500} is one week of Kai's saving, not two.

steps.outcome: The gift is the same as one week of saving, so Kai needs 5 weeks instead of 6. A change can speed a plan up as well as slow it down.
hints: Compare the gift with what Kai saves in a week.
The gift covers some of Kai's weeks. How many?
steps.correct: Right. The gift covers one week, so Kai finishes a week early.

steps.prompt: Ari and Noor each get {m:1000}. Ari saves it for a goal. Noor spends it on a day out. Who chose well?

options.text: Both, if it's what each wanted most
Only Ari, because saving is always right
options.feedback: Not quite. Saving is useful, but spending on something you value is fine too.

options.text: Only Noor, because money is for spending
options.feedback: Not quite. Spending is fine, but so is saving for later. Each gave up something different.

hints: What did each of them give up?
Ari gave up a day out now. Noor gave up progress on a goal.
steps.correct: Right. Each choice gives something up. A good choice is one that fits what you care about.
